newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine lets hryvnia currency find market rate.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine lets hryvnia currency find market rate.

text.p: Ukraine's central bank has ceased supporting the hryvnia on the currency exchange to allow the new monetary unit to find its own level, a top bank official said on Thursday.
"The level has to be determined by the market," Mykola Melnychuk, chief of foreign currency reserves, told Reuters.
The bank stopped selling dollars and started buying them this week. Melnychuk said the policy contributed to a sharp increase in dollar demand and the hryvnia's recent slip.
The hryvnia stood at 1.770 to the dollar on the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange on Thursday, after remaining at 1.76 to the dollar since its formal debut last month.
It exhibited its first drop, to 1.7740, on Monday, edged up to 1.768 on Tuesday and was at 1.769 on Wednesday.
The hryvnia replaced the karbovanets, which was removed from circulation on September 16 after the hryvnia's introduction on September 2. One hryvnia equalled 100,000 karbovanets.
The bank official said it was difficult to predict the hryvnia's future level.
"It depends on how capital will move in and out of Ukraine," he said. "The movement of capital depends upon a stable economy."
He said Ukraine was in talks with the International Monetary Fund to peg the hryvnia to a hard currency or to a basket of currencies, and to make it eventually convertible.
He said the central bank spent $200 million from mid-August -- when demand for the dollar fell in expectation of the hryvnia's introduction -- until October 4.
The central bank has sought to maintain the hryvnia at 1.76 to the dollar to prove the new unit was stable and a success.
It wanted to maintain calm among Ukrainians, who remembered the sharp devaluation of the karbovanets after it was brought in.

Melnychuk said demand for dollars had also increased because a large quantity of money circulating in the shadow economy was removed during the September 2-16 currency replacement period. -- Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
